questions.question:
Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank.

Wedding is an auspicious _______ for all.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**occasion**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**occasion**" refers to a particular event or celebration, often of importance or significance.
 
• In the given sentence, a "**wedding**" is described as an auspicious event, making "occasion" the appropriate and correctly spelled word.
 
• Spelling variations like "occassion", "occation", and "ocassion" are incorrect and commonly confused misspellings.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Wedding is an auspicious **occasion**__ for all.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Occassion** – Incorrect; has an extra "s".
 
• **Occation** – Incorrect; incorrect vowel usage.
 
• **Ocassion** – Incorrect; missing a "c".

questions.question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Sarah and Fidaa entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

options.text: Sarah and Fidaa are entering into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa had entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa were entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Sarah and Fidaa will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **simple past tense**: “entered into an agreement.”
 
• To change it to the **simple future tense**, the correct structure is: **Subject + will + base verb**.
 
• In this case: “Sarah and Fidaa **will enter** into an agreement...” correctly indicates an action that is expected to happen in the future.
 
• The phrase “that are currently accessible” remains unchanged as it refers to present conditions.

Correct sentence: *Sarah and Fidaa **will enter** into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "are entering"** – Present continuous tense, not future.
 
• **Option 3: "had entered"** – Past perfect tense, refers to an action completed before another past action.
 
• **Option 4: "were entered"** – Grammatically incorrect; “entered” is not used in passive voice with “were” in this context.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Mary is the __quieter__ student of the class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. quietest .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When comparing one individual against all others in a group, the **superlative** form is used, which is formed by adding "**-est**" to the word.
 
• The sentence refers to Mary being compared with the rest of the class, implying the need for the superlative form "**quietest**."
 
• The given sentence incorrectly uses "quieter," which is the **comparative **form used for comparing two entities, not one against a group.

Correct sentence: *Mary is the **quietest** student of the class.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**

 
 
• Used to compare two entities.
 
• Formed by adding "**-er**" to single-syllable adjectives (e.g., quieter) or by using "more" for multi-syllable adjectives (e.g., more beautiful).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Used to compare one entity against a group.
 
• Formed by adding "**-est**" to single-syllable adjectives (e.g., quietest) or by using "most" for multi-syllable adjectives (e.g., most beautiful).

questions.question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate degree of adjective.

options.text: She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct way to express the highest degree of comparison **(superlative degree)** is by using **"the most + adjective"** for adjectives that are longer than one syllable.
 
• Option 4, "She is the most talented musician in the orchestra," is grammatically correct and expresses the idea appropriately.
 
• Other options contain grammatical errors:
 
 
• **Option 1:** "She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra" is incorrect because "talent" is a noun, not a comparative adjective.
 
• **Option 2:** "She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra" is incorrect because "talentedest" is not a valid English word.
 
• **Option 3:** "She is more talented musician in the orchestra" is incorrect as it requires "the" before "more talented" to complete the comparison.
 
 

Correct sentence: *She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• Used to compare two things or people.
 
• For one-syllable adjectives, add "-er" (e.g., taller, smarter).
 
• For longer adjectives, use "more + adjective" (e.g., more talented, more beautiful).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• Used to compare one thing or person against all others in a group.
 
• For one-syllable adjectives, add "-est" (e.g., tallest, smartest).
 
• For longer adjectives, use "the most + adjective" (e.g., the most talented, the most beautiful).

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. old much .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'old much'** in the sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• In English, adjectives of age, like "old," are modified by the adverb **'too'** (e.g., "too old").
 
• The correct phrase should be **'too old'** instead of **'old much'**.
 
• The corrected sentence would read: *"Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now."*

Correct sentence: *Ms. Malathi is **too old** to join a college now.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Errors in Adjective Usage:**

 
 
• Using adverbs like 'much' or 'very' incorrectly with adjectives.
 
• For example, we say "too old," "very old," or "extremely old," but not "old much."
 
 
 
• **When to Use 'Too':**
 
 
• 'Too' is used to indicate excessiveness and is followed by an adjective or adverb.
 
• Example: "The bag is too heavy to carry."

questions.question:
Select the correct indefinite article to fill in the blank.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this question, the blank requires an **indefinite article**.
 
• The word **"passionate" **starts with a **consonant sound**. However, the word "photographer" does not affect the choice of the article.
 
• Indefinite articles "a" and "an" are used before singular nouns. The choice depends on whether the following word starts with a vowel sound or consonant sound.
 
• The word "passionate" starts with a **consonant** sound, so the correct indefinite article is **"a."**

Correct sentence: *My neighbour is **a passionate photographer**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"a":** Used before words starting with consonant sounds (e.g., "a cat," "a dog").
